abstract.para: A minimal &agama; profile is a JSON file with three required sections: product identifies what to install, the registration fields activate the subscription, and root sets the administrator credentials. &agama; applies its defaults to everything else. Add a host name, a non-root user and localization settings to produce a profile that installs a usable system without any interaction.

section.title: Generating a profile from an interactive installation
section.para: Instead of writing a profile by hand, you can configure a system interactively through the &agama; Web-based interface or CLI, then capture the resulting configuration as a profile to reuse for future automated installations of similar systems.

step.para: Start the &agama; installer and configure the system interactively: product, storage, network, users, and any other section you need. Do not start the installation yet.

Review profile.json, and remove or adjust anything specific to this one machine, such as a static host name or address, before reusing it for other installations.

section.para: The saved profile can then be loaded like any other, either with agama config load during another interactive session, or by pointing inst.auto at it for an unattended installation.

section.title: Summary of creating a profile
section.para: With the sections above in place, you have a working &agama; profile that installs &productname; with a host name, a non-root user, and basic localization settings. Add further sections, such as storage, network, or software, as your deployment requires, or generate a starting point automatically from an interactive installation with agama config show.
